prompt: What can a plain directory of Parquet files not do? Choose all that apply.
hint: Four gaps were named.

choices.text: Show the table as it was yesterday
choices.why: Yes. An overwritten file is gone.

choices.text: Store each column apart
choices.why: Parquet does that on its own.

choices.text: Be read by Spark
choices.why: Spark reads it every lesson.

choices.text: Make a write visible all at once
choices.why: Yes. A reader can see half of one.

prompt: A nightly append to a Parquet directory ran twice. Why does nothing fail?
hint: What does a reader of the directory take?

choices.text: A reader takes every file it finds there
choices.why: Right, and the second run's files look like any others.

choices.text: Spark removes duplicate rows when it reads Parquet
choices.why: It does not; the count doubled.

choices.text: The second run replaced the first one's files
choices.why: Append adds; six files were there.

choices.text: Parquet files carry a run number that readers check
choices.why: There is no such number in them.

prompt: What makes a Delta commit atomic?
hint: What is the last thing a writer creates?

choices.text: Parquet files are written in a single block
choices.why: Files are written first, where no reader looks.

choices.text: Writers take a lock on the table's directory
choices.why: There are no locks: the check is at the end.

choices.text: The driver holds every data file in memory until commit
choices.why: Executors write the data files directly.

choices.text: Creating a given log file succeeds for one writer only
choices.why: Right. Until it exists, the new data files are invisible.

prompt: Put the steps of a Delta write in order.
hint: The data comes before the commit.
items: Try to create the next numbered log file
If the number is taken, check what changed
Retry with the next number if nothing conflicts

prompt: `spark-submit --___ ~/lib/a.jar,~/lib/b.jar job.py` hands those files to the driver and to every executor.
hint: Four letters.

prompt: Why did the second attempt to append February write nothing?
hint: What did the first attempt record in the log?

choices.text: February had been deleted in between
choices.why: The count stayed at 154,822.

choices.text: Delta refuses any append of rows already in the table
choices.why: It compares no rows; without the pair it would have doubled them.

choices.text: The log already had that job id and run number
choices.why: Right. That is `txnAppId` and `txnVersion`.

choices.text: The table was locked by the first attempt
choices.why: Delta takes no locks.

prompt: Why did one `DELETE` remove six files and add three?
hint: Can a Parquet file be edited?

choices.text: Each deleted row is written to a file of its own
choices.why: Three files for 6,285 rows.

choices.text: The delete also compacted the table
choices.why: Compaction is `OPTIMIZE`.

choices.text: Delta keeps two copies of every file
choices.why: It keeps one; old ones stay for history.

choices.text: Files are rewritten without the deleted rows
choices.why: Right. The commit lists both sets.

prompt: After the delete, how could `VERSION AS OF 1` still return 154,822 purchases?
hint: Where are the removed files?

choices.text: The count comes from the CSV files of the raw layer
choices.why: The table knows nothing of the raw layer.

choices.text: Delta keeps a backup in the driver's memory
choices.why: Nothing is kept in memory between runs.

choices.text: The delete was only applied to newer files
choices.why: It applied to every file with the crawler's rows.

choices.text: The removed files are still on disk, and version 1 lists them
choices.why: Right, until a vacuum deletes them.

prompt: Match each command to what it does.
hint: Only one of them deletes files from disk.

pairs.right: Rewrites small files into large ones in a new commit
Deletes files no version within the retention needs
Lists the commits and what each one did

right_distractors: Copies the table to another catalogue

prompt: Why does `VACUUM` refuse a retention shorter than seven days unless a check is switched off?
hint: Who might still be using an old version?

choices.text: Files younger than seven days are still being written
choices.why: A committed file is finished.

choices.text: The log can only be rewritten once a week
choices.why: The log is appended to at every commit.

choices.text: Deleting files costs money on a local disk
choices.why: Deleting is free; losing history is the cost.

choices.text: A query still reading an old version would lose its files
choices.why: Right. Version 0 could not be read afterwards.

prompt: After `OPTIMIZE` and before `VACUUM`, how many data files were on disk for the 31 daily appends?
hint: The old files and the new one.

prompt: What does Iceberg's hidden partitioning by `days(ts)` let a query do?
hint: Did the query mention a partition?

choices.text: Write a `day` column the table did not have
choices.why: No `day` column is ever written.

choices.text: Filter on `ts` and still skip whole days
choices.why: Right. Two files read, 58 skipped.

choices.text: Skip the footer of every Parquet file it reads
choices.why: Footers are still read for the files it keeps.

choices.text: Read the table without any catalogue
choices.why: The catalogue finds the table.

prompt: Why did January come out as 32 files, one per partition?
hint: In which time zone does `days(ts)` cut?

choices.text: It cuts UTC days, which local days straddle
choices.why: Right. São Paulo is three hours behind.

choices.text: The first file holds the table's metadata
choices.why: Metadata lives in its own directory.

choices.text: One of the days was too large to fit in a single file
choices.why: A day's purchases are a few hundred kilobytes.

choices.text: 2025 has an extra day in January
choices.why: January has 31 days every year.

prompt: Order Iceberg's metadata from the catalogue's pointer down to the data.
hint: Each points to the next.

prompt: The upsert batch held 1,000 corrections and all of February. How many purchases did the table end with?
hint: Corrections replace rows; new rows are added.

choices.text: February only, since the write replaced the table
choices.why: An upsert keeps what it does not touch.

choices.text: January plus February plus the 1,000 corrections
choices.why: The corrections replaced rows with the same key.

choices.text: January plus February, each purchase once
January only, since corrections cancel the batch
choices.why: Both kinds of row were applied.

prompt: Match each Hudi table type to its trade.
hint: One writes Parquet only; one also writes logs.

pairs.right: Rewrites changed files: dear writes, plain reads
Logs changes beside the files: cheap writes, dearer reads

prompt: A Hudi commit passes through `requested`, then `___`, then completed.
hint: In flight.

prompt: Match each situation to the format it suits best.
hint: Choose by what reads and writes the table.

pairs.left: Read by Spark, Trino, Flink and a cloud warehouse
A stream of corrections every few minutes
Read only by Spark, with the least to set up

prompt: Match each problem to the feature of a table format that fixes it.
hint: Each came from a section of this lesson.

pairs.left: A retried job doubles a day
pairs.right: An idempotent write with a job id and run number

pairs.left: A visitor asks to be forgotten
pairs.right: A `DELETE` that rewrites the files holding the rows

pairs.left: A report must be rerun as of last Monday
pairs.right: Time travel to an older version

pairs.left: Thousands of small files from daily appends

prompt: What does a table format not do by itself?
hint: Lesson 10's choices are made underneath.

choices.text: Keep a history of versions
choices.why: All three keep one.

choices.text: Delete rows with one statement
choices.why: `DELETE` did it here.

choices.text: Make queries faster
choices.why: Right. Codec, types and sort order still decide that.

choices.text: Make a write visible all at once
choices.why: That is exactly what the log does.
